blocks.title: Know what a package does before you install it
blocks.description: Drop an APK, IPA, DEX, shared library, executable or archive into the workspace and get a readable verdict: what it is, what it asks for, what it hides, and how much it deserves your trust.

items.title: Format-aware facts
items.description: One pass recognises Android packages and bundles, iOS apps, ELF, PE, Mach-O, raw DEX and plain archives, then reports architecture, entry point, size, entropy and SHA-256.

items.title: Manifest and permission review
items.description: Reads the binary AndroidManifest inside the APK: package identity, SDK range, debuggable and backup flags, exported components and every requested permission.

items.title: Native hardening checks
items.description: Flags writable+executable segments, executable stacks, missing PIE or NX, packer signatures and stripped tooling — the differences that decide how hard a library is to attack.

items.title: Evidence, not guesses
items.description: Runtime-loading, shell execution, reflection, weak crypto and credential-shaped strings are reported with the exact strings and offsets that triggered them.

items.title: One score you can defend
items.description: Each rule carries a severity and a weight, so the 0-100 risk score and A-E grade can be traced back to named rule ids instead of a black box.

items.title: Reports that leave the app
items.description: Copy the markdown, or save markdown or JSON through the system dialog to attach to a review, a ticket or an internal security note.

showcase.user_prompt: Why does this APK score 62? Which risky permissions does it ask for?
showcase.assistant_reply:
62 (grade D) is driven by three rules:

| Rule | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apk.exported-component` | High | 3 activities/services are exported with no permission guard |
| `apk.dynamic-loading` | High | `DexClassLoader` appears in the DEX, so the real logic is unpacked at runtime |
| `apk.dangerous-permission` | Medium | Requests `READ_SMS`, `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`, `READ_CONTACTS` |

It also has no v2/v3 signature, only the legacy META-INF signature. Re-download it from the official channel; if you must keep analysing, dump the runtime-loaded dex first and review that code instead.

items.title: Open the Hanshuang Pojia tab
items.description: In a project conversation, add the panel from the activity tab bar. It lists the packages and binaries already in the workspace folder.

items.title: Pick a sample or paste a path
items.description: Click a file in the list, or type any path. Project files up to 32 MiB go to the local engine; anything larger, or outside the project folder, is handed to the agent in one click. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is executed.

items.title: Read the report
items.description: Risk score, the findings that drove it, manifest facts and per-section details. Switch between Summary and Full, then copy or save the report.

blocks.content: The activity-bar tab is now a fourteen-page workbench: Workbench, Guide, Documents, Samples, Findings, Strings, Disassembly, Manifest, Entropy, Signature, Compare, Self check, Reports and Settings. Every page reads the same report, so a sample you analyse once stays inspectable from every angle — including a report-to-report diff of two builds. Two pages stand on their own: Disassembly walks the sample's own executable sections, ranks candidate functions and renders one at a time as a control-flow listing in summary, branches-only or full density, cut at a character budget; Documents renders the 309 field write-ups, manuals and tool docs the plugin ships byte for byte, with in-memory title search and on-demand full-text search, each body loaded as its own build chunk. Purple buttons send an English prompt to the conversation, and a report produced by the agent in chat appears back in the panel with a "from chat" marker. Settings can switch analysis mode, disable individual rules and change scan resolution; storage is optional and the panel degrades to session-only memory when the host has not granted it.

Code-level questions go through the agent: `list_code_symbols` reads ELF, PE and Mach-O symbol and export tables, `disassemble_range` sweeps an AArch64 or x86 byte range, `search_dex_symbols` finds classes, methods and strings in a DEX or APK, and `diff_binaries` shows what changed between two builds. Every listing is a linear sweep with file offsets - never decompiled source, and never a claim about what runs.

The bundled agent document carries the workbench kit 2.0 protocol as its fifth part: lab mode entered with `lab：` and left with `退出实验`, the deployment and verification board driven by `setup/verify.ps1 -Detailed`, knowledge-base-first recon, and the `seep` (23 tools) / `ida` (~243) MCP matrix with its Radare2 fallback table. Since 2.1 the kit's skill library ships with it - 165 files, 2.4 MB, byte-identical to the upstream tree, routed by path from the protocol. It is payload and documentation, not a dependency: the panel above still runs with no external toolchain, and nothing here is installed behind your back.

This is static triage, not proof of safety. Android signature digests are read, not cryptographically verified; packed or encrypted code is reported as a hint and never unpacked; behaviour that only shows up at runtime stays invisible here. Treat a low score as "nothing obvious", not as an approval. Two hard limits come from the host, not the plugin: the panel can only read files inside the open project folder, and at most 32 MiB per file. Bigger or out-of-project samples are still analysable — the panel hands them to the chat agent, which has the app's own file access.
